The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test `testNestedWithCommentsJDOM` expects that when accessing XML values, leading and trailing spaces should be preserved. The current bug report confirms that JXPath currently trims string values automatically, resulting in losing leading/trailing spaces. The key code snippet responsible for this behavior is the `getValue()` method in the `JDOMNodePointer` class.

In this method, various node types such as `Element`, `Comment`, `Text`, and `CDATA` retrieve their textual content through calls to `getTextTrim()`, or explicitly call `trim()` on the string values before returning them. For example:
- `Element` nodes return `getTextTrim()`, which by contract returns the text with whitespace trimmed.
- `Comment` nodes retrieve the text and then explicitly call `trim()` before returning.
- `Text` and `CDATA` nodes also return trimmed text.
- The `ProcessingInstruction` node also trims its data string before returning.

This means all string values retrieved through this method will have their leading and trailing whitespace stripped off before being returned to the caller, causing the observed bug: when an XML element value has leading or trailing spaces, those spaces are removed unexpectedly.

Thus, the root cause of the bug is that `JDOMNodePointer.getValue()` uses trimming methods or explicitly trims values before returning text content. This behavior contradicts expected behavior according to the test case and bug report, which want leading/trailing spaces preserved.

Since this method is responsible for retrieving node values in JXPath's XML model for JDOM, adjusting it to not trim texts (or only trim when explicitly needed) would fix the issue.

No relevant recent bug reports are available, so only the current report, test case, and code snippet are used for this diagnosis.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
